tool_input.command: head -20 node_modules/@guren/inertia-client/dist/index.js; echo "=== chunk imports ==="; for f in node_modules/@guren/inertia-client/dist/chunk-*.js; do echo "-- $f"; grep -n '^import\|from "' $f | grep -o 'from "[^"]*"' | sort -u | head -10; done
git --no-pager diff -- src/app.ts app/Http/Controllers/Auth resources/js/pages/auth/Login.tsx | head -60

result:
Done — `bun run typecheck` is clean and `bun test` passes (21 tests across 3 files, including 19 new ones).

I moved the auth pages' copy into the translation catalog and added the Japanese side of it. `lang/en/auth.json` now holds the English login/register strings verbatim as they read today, `lang/ja/auth.json` mirrors it key-for-key with the requested Japanese, and `lang/ja/messages.json` translates the existing welcome message as `:nameへようこそ！` with its placeholder intact (`bunx guren check --i18n` reports full parity on both sides, and `.guren/translations.gen.ts` was regenerated). `src/app.ts` now declares `i18n: { supported: ['en', 'ja'] }`, which is all Guren needs to detect the locale from `?locale=`, the locale cookie, or `Accept-Language` (with English as the fallback for `en`, no header, or unsupported languages such as `fr`) and to share the matching catalog with the page. `resources/js/pages/auth/Login.tsx` and `Register.tsx` now pull every label, heading, button, and `<Head title>` through a `useTranslation()` hook, and `LoginController`/`RegisterController` pass `this.t('auth.*.title')` as the document title so the pre-hydration `<title>` is localized too. The hook lives in a new `resources/js/lib/useTranslation.ts` rather than being imported from `@guren/inertia-client`: the dev server's import map points that bare specifier at the vendored client entry, which exports only `startInertiaClient`, so importing the framework hook there would break page hydration in the browser — the local hook reads the same `_i18n` shared prop with the same lookup/interpolation/fallback semantics and works identically under SSR, dev, and the production Vite build (verified with `bun run build`). `tests/AuthLocalization.test.ts` covers catalog key parity and placeholder survival, plus both pages rendered through the app's own SSR entry for `ja`, `ja-JP`, a full Japanese browser header, and the English/no-header/`fr` cases.
